subject: Materials Science
title: Thermal Degradation of Polymers
description: A fast breakdown of Thermal Degradation of Polymers for builders.

hook.text: Overheat a plastic part and it yellows, smells, and crumbles — the polymer chains are breaking apart.

buildup.text: Thermal degradation breaks polymer chains through random scission or unzipping from chain ends.

discovery.text: Each polymer has a maximum service temperature — PTFE handles 260°C, polyethylene only 80°C.

twist.text: Thermo-oxidative degradation is worse — heat plus oxygen attacks faster than either alone.

climax.text: Antioxidants sacrificially react with oxygen radicals — extending polymer life at elevated temperatures.

punchline.text: Heat breaks polymer chains link by link — the material forgets it was strong.

quiz.question: What is thermo-oxidative degradation?
options: Degradation caused by UV light exposure
Combined attack of heat and oxygen on polymer chains
